title: FAQ
description: Frequently asked questions about the NoMercy Player SDK.
content: faq can i use both the video player and music player on the same page? yes. each player instance is isolated by its id. the video player and music player share no global state beyond the internal instance registry. they do not interfere. you can have both playing at the same time subject to browser audio policy. if you need one to pause when the other plays, wire that coordination yourself in a consumer plugin or in your app code. --- how do i write my own subtitle renderer? replace the built-in vtt text rendering with your own plugin that implements the same interface. register your plugin with . for ass/ssa subtitles with full typesetting, add — it loads dynamically and handles its own rendering. do not combine and a custom renderer for the same subtitle track. see video — subtitle overlay for the full api. --- does the player handle 401 / 403 differently? yes. the auth pipeline treats them differently by design: - 401 — token expired. is called once, the new token is applied, and the request is retried. if refresh fails, an event fires and the request errors. - 403 — access denied. the error propagates immediately. is never called for 403s. the server has denied access even with valid credentials. never lump 401 and 403 in the same catch block. a 403 may signal an entitlement problem that no amount of token refreshing will fix. --- how do i add auto-advance play next track when the current one ends? add — it is shipped with both library packages: the plugin listens to the event and calls . when crossfade is enabled on the music player, it triggers instead. --- how do i pause all players at once? there is no global play/pause. you control each instance by id: if you need coordinated playback across multiple players group listening, use — planned for v2.1. --- can i use the player with typescript strict mode? yes. the packages ship full typescript types. all public methods are typed. the generic parameter or threads your playlist item type through , , , and events — no casts required. --- how do i render the player without the built-in ui? do not add . the player itself renders nothing — all chrome is opt-in through plugins. build your own controls using the event api: --- how do i restrict hls quality to avoid high bitrate on slow networks? is not related to quality. quality selection lives in the video player's hls adapter. set a maximum level via the config: to hard-cap to a specific quality level index at runtime: hdr-aware abr is automatic — on sdr displays, the player filters out hdr levels from the abr selection pool. no configuration needed. see video — hls for the full quality api. --- how do i listen to events from a plugin i did not write? use the string form with the auto-namespaced event name on : plugin events are always namespaced as . the class-form is only available inside a subclass body — it is a method and does not exist on the external surface. --- is the player compatible with capacitor, tauri, or electron? yes, via the platform adapter system. override individual sub-ports without rebuilding the entire bundle: the player's core logic only calls the interfaces — it does not import capacitor or tauri directly. --- where do i report bugs? - nomercy-video-player: github.com/nomercy-entertainment/nomercy-video-player/issues - nomercy-music-player: github.com/nomercy-entertainment/nomercy-music-player/issues - nomercy-player-core: github.com/nomercy-entertainment/nomercy-player-kit/issues

title: Migration Guide — v1 to v2
description: Upgrading from nomercy-video-player or nomercy-music-player v1. What changed, what broke, and how to fix it.
content: migration guide — v1 to v2 this page is the high-level overview. for the full breaking-change tables, go to the per-package guides: - video player: https://github.com/nomercy-entertainment/nomercy-video-player/blob/master/migration.md - music player: https://github.com/nomercy-entertainment/nomercy-music-player/blob/master/migration.md - kit adapter ports + subpath imports: https://github.com/nomercy-entertainment/nomercy-player-kit/blob/master/migration.md why the api changed v2 is a ground-up rewrite on a shared kit . the design goals drove the breaking changes: - event payload extensibility — v1 events carried raw objects and multi-field flat structs. v2 wraps everything: instead of raw , instead of the item alone. adding a field to a v2 event is non-breaking; it was breaking in v1. - overloaded getter/setter pattern — reads, writes. eliminates / pairs. - plugin system replacement — v1 used . v2 uses . class-based plugins enable typescript inference, tree-shaking, and typed cross-plugin events. - opt-in features — eq, spectrum, mediasession, auto-advance were always-on in v1. in v2, they are opt-in plugins. zero cost if you don't add them. --- the top five breaks these affect every v1 consumer: 1. all event payloads changed every call needs updating. examples: 2. / → > this is the silent-break risk. the player will load without error but fail to play anything. music player: → video player: → map the field in your adapter layer: the server api should be updated to emit directly. the field mapping is a bridge until then. 3. plugin api replaced 4. methods renamed | v1 | v2 | | -------------------- | ------------------------ | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | event | event | | event video | event | 5. always-on features are now opt-in plugins --- string → number video v1 was a formatted string like . v2 is a number in seconds. formatters that expected a string will produce . update any component that displays or compares duration: --- event timing v1 music player fired after a hardcoded delay. v2 fires after setup and all plugins resolve. do not rely on timing — always . --- what's new in v2 v2 ships features that did not exist in v1: - cancellable events — - auth pipeline with 401/403 separation and token refresh - pluggable storage backend — swap for indexeddb or a remote api - platform abstraction — native-shell support capacitor, tauri, electron - phase machine — returns a typed phase string - metrics api — , throttled event - hdr-aware abr video — constrains hls.js to sdr on sdr displays - — synced lrc lyrics - — multi-user synchronized playback - — single-tab coordination - — widevine eme - — chromecast handoff - queue operations: , , , , , --- full change tables the per-package migration.md files contain complete tables for every renamed method, every changed event payload, every removed api, and every configuration field change: - nomercy-video-player migration.md - nomercy-music-player migration.md - nomercy-player-kit migration.md

content: nomercy-player-core — kit the kit is layer 2 of the five-layer architecture. it provides the generic infrastructure that both and build on. when to depend on the kit directly most consumers install or — both packages re-export the kit's public api. install directly only if you: - are writing a library-level plugin that must work with both video and music players without importing either - are building a new library package on top of the kit --- kit sections | topic | page | | ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------- | | the adapter ports | adapters | | built-in plugins shipped with the kit | plugins | | typed event system, on/once/off/emit | event system | | 13-phase lifecycle machine | lifecycle | | auth fetch, 401/403, retry | auth & fetch | | i18n adapter and vite plugin | i18n | | error codes, notimplementederror, catch patterns | errors | | playbackmetrics, null-when-unavailable matrix | metrics | | testing subpath stub player | testing | --- architecture context the kit owns nothing above layer 2. it does not import from the library packages and has no knowledge of or .

title: Subtitle Overlay
description: The SubtitleOverlayPlugin: VTT subtitle rendering, styling, and accessibility (FCC 47 CFR 79.4, WCAG 1.4.4).
content: / source: packages/nomercy-video-player-v2/src/plugins/subtitle-overlay/index.ts / renders the player's webvtt subtitle cue stream as a positioned dom overlay above the video element. register it whenever you serve vtt subtitle tracks. for ass/ssa files use instead, this plugin handles vtt only. plugin id import what it does renders the player's event stream as a positioned dom overlay above the video element. it is a pure consumer, all subtitle parsing, vtt fetching, and cue tracking live in the kit. the overlay subscribes to the single event and renders one per active cue. features: - one box per active cue, pooled and reused, no dom churn - webvtt cue layout: , , , and attributes from the vtt cue are applied as css positioning - collision detection, when two cues would overlap, the later one is displaced along the line axis - overlay is letterbox-fit to the actual video display rectangle not the container, so cue font size scales with the visible picture, not the player shell - settings font family, size, color, edge style, background are applied and update live on events - language tag is mirrored onto for css targeting for ass/ssa subtitle files, add the octopusplugin instead, this overlay handles vtt only. options takes no options. all subtitle style settings font family, size, color, edge style, background are driven by the adapter and the api at runtime. registration dom structure the plugin mounts: subtitle style the overlay respects all fields of via : changes are applied immediately to all active cue areas without re-rendering. track selection api the event fires when the active track changes: subtitle cue stream the player emits events as active cues change. this is the low-level cue stream useful for custom renderers: style persistence user style preferences font size, color, background opacity are persisted via the adapter. the default writes to . accessibility the overlay is built around two formal standards, plus a few implementation choices that follow from them. caption placement fcc 47 cfr 79.4 the wrapper insets captions 5% from the top and bottom and 3% from the left and right of the actual video picture, not the player frame. a letterbox-fits that safezone to the real video display rectangle and re-fits on fullscreen changes, so the inset always tracks the picture. pillarboxed 4:3 content gets 3% of the 4:3 picture, not 3% of the wider 16:9 shell. this keeps captions clear of player chrome and device bezels so they stay viewable in their entirety, which is what fcc 47 cfr 79.4 requires, and it matches the placement you see on netflix, youtube, and apple tv+. resizable text wcag 2.1 sc 1.4.4, level aa caption text is sized with . the unit scales with the player's width, so captions grow with the video and follow browser zoom without losing legibility. the value comes from the user's own font-size preference, so anyone who needs bigger text can get it without leaving the player. the 14px floor keeps captions readable even on the smallest players, and the 56px ceiling stops them from swallowing the screen. that satisfies wcag 2.1 sc 1.4.4 resize text: caption text scales well past 200% without losing content. right-to-left text both the cue area and the cue text carry . the browser then applies the unicode bidirectional algorithm to each cue's own content, so arabic, hebrew, and mixed-script subtitles render in the correct direction with no per-language setup. contrast the subtitle style system ships five edge effects drop shadow, uniform outline, depressed, raised, and a stacked shadow that users combine with their own text and background colours. the stacked-shadow preset layers several black shadows into a strong outline that holds up against whatever video sits behind it. the plugin does not compute a fixed contrast ratio for you, because video backgrounds keep changing, but these controls give users what they need to meet wcag 1.4.3 on their own content. screen readers the overlay is visual only. it carries no region and no , so assistive technology does not announce the caption text, and screen reader users are expected to follow the audio track itself. if your app needs on-screen captions announced, add and to the element. see also - octopus plugin ass/ssa - subtitle style store adapter - cycling methods, cyclesubtitles - troubleshooting, subtitles not appearing

title: Octopus (ASS/SSA)
description: OctopusPlugin: libass-based ASS/SSA subtitle rendering via a WASM worker, with auth-gated font loading and graceful degradation.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-video-player-v2/src/plugins/octopus/index.ts / octopus ass/ssa is the plugin to reach for when your media library includes anime or any content with styled or subtitle tracks. it wraps the nomercy fork of libass-wasm and handles the lifecycle, font loading, and auth-gating so the wasm worker never touches the network directly. for plain subtitle tracks, use instead. is a plain dependency bundled with the package. the plugin imports it dynamically at runtime as a safety net. when the import fails the plugin logs a warning and marks itself as degraded; playback continues normally and ass/ssa subtitles will not render. plugin id: options | option | type | default | description | | ------ | ---- | ------- | ----------- | | | | bundled path | url for the modern wasm worker script. | | | | none | url for the legacy non-wasm worker, for browsers without webassembly. | | | | none | font url used when a requested font is not in the item's fonts list. | | | | | static font urls preloaded for every item, supplementing per-item fonts. | | | | library default | renderer target fps. leave unset to let the library choose. | | | | library default wasm-blend | render quality vs. performance trade-off. leave unset for the library default. | | | | | fetch subtitle chunks lazily, useful for very large ass files. | | | | library default | internal scaler ratio. leave unset for default scaling. | | | | | frames pre-computed ahead of . higher values smooth playback through heavy ass effects at the cost of memory. | | | | | enable debug logging in the libass wasm worker. | --- events events fire on the plugin channel. subscribe from outside the plugin using the string form. | event | payload | description | | ----- | ------- | ----------- | | | | fired after the libass renderer initialises and the first frame is ready for the given subtitle url. | --- methods subtitle read or set the active subtitle url directly, bypassing the kit's track list. use this for ass files the consumer supplies outside the array. fonts read or replace the plugin-level static font list. the getter returns blob: urls when fonts have already been fetched and loaded for the active item, or the original plugin-level url strings before the first load. calling it with new urls clears the per-item font cache and re-loads the active subtitle so the new fonts apply immediately. renderer returns the raw libass renderer handle for advanced consumers. the returned value is an opaque object; its type is not part of the public api. the plugin retains lifecycle ownership, do not call on the returned instance directly. --- font resolution fonts are resolved in this order for each item: 1. the array on the active . each entry is a object whose property is a manifest url or a direct font file url. 2. , static urls registered at plugin level, applied to all items. 3. , a single url used when ass requests a font not found above. all font fetches go through the kit's auth pipeline. each binary is converted to a blob url and passed to the wasm worker. blob urls are revoked when the renderer is torn down to avoid memory leaks. --- registration --- see also - subtitleoverlay plugin, vtt subtitle rendering - videoplaylistitem, fonts field - troubleshooting, subtitles not appearing

title: Touch Zones
description: TouchZonesPlugin: mobile tap-to-seek, double-tap controls, and touch-friendly play/pause overlay.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-video-player-v2/src/plugins/touch-zones/index.ts / touch zones renders a transparent tap-zone overlay that intercepts touch events before they reach the video element. register it when you expect touch or hybrid pointer/touch input, typically on mobile browsers or touch-screen deployments. it gives you double-tap to seek on the left and right edges, single-tap to toggle controls visibility, and centre double-tap to toggle fullscreen. plugin id what it does the plugin mounts a css grid overlay at , above the video element but below the desktopui controls overlay at . touch and click events on the zones are intercepted before they reach the video, but control buttons on the desktop-ui layer remain clickable above. layout | column | content | | ----------- | --------------------------------- | | left third | seek backward zone | | centre | play/pause and fullscreen zone | | right third | seek forward zone | on mobile detected via or , two extra zones appear in the centre column: rows 1-2 for volume up and rows 5-6 for volume down. the play/pause zone compresses to rows 3-5 on mobile. tap behaviour | zone | single tap | double tap | | -------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------ | | left | hide controls only if visible | seek backward | | right | hide controls only if visible | seek forward | | centre desktop | toggle play/pause | toggle fullscreen | | centre mobile | toggle play/pause if controls shown | toggle fullscreen | | volume up mobile | hide controls only if visible | volume up | | volume down mobile | hide controls only if visible | volume down | single-tap on the left and right zones only hides controls; it never shows them. when controls are hidden the container's own touchstart event wakes them, not a zone tap. on desktop non-touch, the centre single-tap always toggles play/pause regardless of controls visibility. seek feedback indicator each seek zone shows a floating circular indicator on double-tap containing a chevron icon and a cumulative label for example after three rapid taps. the indicator collapses around one second after the last tap in a burst. rapid successive taps update the same element rather than stacking new ones. css transitions on and drive the show/hide animation with no javascript animation frames. --- options | option | type | default | description | | ---------------------- | --------- | ------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | | | | maximum milliseconds between taps for double-tap detection. | | | | | deprecated. use . when both are set, takes precedence for backwards compatibility. | | | | | seconds to seek on a double-tap. | | | | | when , single-tap on the centre zone never toggles playback. mirror this on if you also use that plugin. | --- registration register after so the layering is correct. --- integration with desktopui emits to tell to hide the controls overlay. you do not need to wire this yourself; the two plugins coordinate via the shared event automatically. this plugin only emits the hide direction . the show direction is triggered by the container's own touchstart handler, not by this plugin. if you use on , pass the same option to . both plugins register their own click handlers desktop-ui on the video element, touch-zones on the overlay zones and each needs the switch independently. --- see also - desktop ui plugin - key handler plugin - tv ui plugin

content: / source: packages/nomercy-video-player-v2/src/plugins/live-transcoding/index.ts / live transcoding plugin id: is for when your backend encodes video on-demand, segment by segment, and the player needs to know the transcoder's progress before it seeks or starts loading. it opens a websocket to a transcoding control endpoint, and gates and until the server reports that the requested position is already encoded. without a or the plugin is entirely inert: no connections are opened and no gates are applied, so it is safe to register in all configurations. what it does the plugin connects to your server over websocket and listens for job status messages. on it resets progress state and waits for the server to confirm at least position 0 is ready. on it checks whether the seek target is ahead of the transcoder's write head, and if so it waits up to milliseconds before releasing the player. the current write head position is exposed through the method, updated live from server progress messages. options | option | type | default | description | | ------ | ---- | ------- | ----------- | | | | none | websocket url of the transcoding control endpoint. | | | | none | alias for . either one works; title: Tab Leader
description: TabLeaderPlugin uses the Web Locks API to ensure only one tab plays at a time on the same origin.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-player-kit/src/plugins/tab-leader/index.ts, re-exported verbatim from nomercy-video-player / tab leader solves a specific annoyance: you open your library in two browser tabs and both start playing at once. the plugin uses the browser's web locks api to hold a named lock while a tab is playing. only one tab holds the lock at a time. when a second tab requests it, the browser queues that request and hands the lock over the moment the first tab releases it or closes. reach for this plugin whenever you need to guarantee that only one player instance on the same origin is active at a time. if you want finer control, such as scoping leadership to a single player instance rather than the whole origin, pass a factory in the options. plugin id: options | option | type | default | description | | ------ | ---- | ------- | ----------- | | | | | action taken when this tab loses the leader lock. calls . calls so audio stops but buffering continues. | | | | | re-request the lock whenever the tab becomes visible via . set explicitly to to disable; absence is treated as . | | | | | factory returning the lock key. when absent, the plugin falls back to the shared key , which is global across all instances on the same origin. return a per-player or per-session string to scope leadership more narrowly. | --- events | event | payload | description | | ----- | ------- | ----------- | | | | this tab now holds the lock and is the active player. | | | | lock released voluntarily via or when the plugin disposes. | | | | web locks not available in this environment. the plugin is inert. | --- methods isleader returns when this tab currently holds the leader lock. requestlock queue a lock-acquire request. the returned promise resolves when the lock is released via , plugin disposal, or tab close, not when it is first acquired. calling while an election is already in progress returns the existing pending promise rather than starting a second one. releaselock voluntarily release the leader lock. emits when this tab was the leader. the next queued tab acquires the lock immediately. no-ops if this tab is not currently the leader. requestleadership / releaseleadership backwards-compatible aliases for and . resolves to when leadership is held after the attempt, otherwise. prefer the non-alias names in new code. --- registration scoping to a specific player by default the lock key is global to the origin, so one tab plays at a time across all player instances on that origin. pass to scope it to a server id, content item, or session: reading leader state --- see also - message plugin - embed plugin - player kit plugins

title: Embed
description: EmbedPlugin adds a postMessage control bridge to a player running inside an iframe, letting the parent page send commands and receive events without shared JavaScript.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-player-kit/src/plugins/embed/index.ts, re-exported verbatim from nomercy-video-player-v2/src/plugins/embed/index.ts / embed register when you drop the player into a third-party page, a cms widget, or a no-code builder via an . the plugin wires up a channel so the parent page can send commands play, pause, seek, and more and listen for player events, all without any shared javascript context between the two pages. if the player is not inside an , this plugin does nothing harmful, but you do not need it for that case. plugin id import what it does on , the plugin attaches a listener to and subscribes to the configured set of player events. inbound messages that match are validated against and dispatched to the appropriate player method. player events are packaged as and posted back to the host page via . the listener and all event forwarders are cleaned up automatically on . options | option | type | default | description | | ------ | ---- | ------- | ----------- | | | | none | origins allowed to send messages. empty means all inbound commands are rejected. accepts any origin development only. | | | | | player events to forward to the host page as messages. | | | | | declared in the options interface but not yet read by the implementation. has no effect at runtime. | embedcommand commands sent from the parent page to the embedded player all use as the envelope: | command | description | | ------- | ----------- | | | calls | | | calls | | | calls | | | seeks to seconds | | | sets volume to 0-100 | | | mutes audio | | | unmutes audio | | | advances to next queue item | | | returns to previous queue item | unknown commands are logged as warnings via and silently dropped. embedeventmessage every forwarded message has the envelope . the player's real event payload is the value. extra fields described below are properties of , not top-level fields on the message. | forwarded name | shape | description | | -------------- | ------------ | ----------- | | | | player has initialised | | | | playback started | | | | playback paused | | | | track finished | | | | periodic time update. is the current position in seconds. | page methods updating via or the method takes effect immediately on the next inbound message. security note when exactly one origin is in the allowlist, outbound calls are pinned to that origin. when multiple origins are listed or is used, outbound messages target . pin to a single origin in production for best security. required iframe attributes for full functionality the needs: the permission is load-bearing. without it never activates, so os-level controls lock screen, now playing, bluetooth do not appear even when is also registered. registration see also - player kit, built-in plugins title: Audio Graph
description: AudioGraphPlugin owns the Web Audio signal chain and is the required foundation for EqualizerPlugin, MixerPlugin, SpectrumPlugin, and CanvasPlugin.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-player-kit/src/plugins/audio-graph/index.ts, re-exported from nomercy-video-player / audio graph is the foundation for every web audio feature in the player. register it before , , , or . it creates the , connects the backend's audio output into the web audio graph, and owns the signal chain that downstream plugins extend. without , the other web audio plugins are inert. plugin id import what it does on the plugin creates or reuses an and connects the backend's audio output into the graph. when the backend exposes an , the plugin reuses that node as the chain source rather than calling a second time. browsers silently stop routing audio if the same media element is wrapped twice. subsequent plugins extend the chain by calling or the / shorthands. the chain topology looks like this: the starts in state per browser autoplay policy. the plugin resumes it on the first event, which always fires inside or immediately after a user gesture. options | option | type | default | description | | ------ | ---- | ------- | ----------- | | | | | latency hint for the . use for video and music, when round-trip latency matters. | | | | | fft size for the shared . higher values give finer frequency resolution at the cost of time resolution. | | | | | smoothing time constant 0 to 1 for the shared analyser. higher values make spectrum output lag more behind transients. | events | event | payload | description | | ----- | ------- | ----------- | | | | is live and the baseline chain is connected. | | | | context closed on dispose. | | | | effect list changed; downstream plugins re-link their own nodes. | | | | unavailable in this environment; plugin is inert. | methods these are the public methods you call from consumer code or from other plugins via . registration register before any other web audio plugin. the required layering order is first, then , , , or in any order after. see also - plugin registration - player kit plugins reference - music player audiographplugin

title: Cycling Methods
description: cycleSubtitles and cycleAudioTracks.
content: / source: packages/nomercy-video-player-v2/src/types.ts ivideoplayer / cyclesubtitles walks the subtitle track list in order: . each call activates the next track; when the end is reached it cycles back to off. this method is designed for remote-control contexts keyboard, tv d-pad where the user cannot pick from a dropdown menu. ui plugins that render a subtitle menu should call directly instead. the keyhandlerplugin binds , , and the media key to by default. emits: with the newly selected track index or when cycling to off. cycleaudiotracks walks the audio track list in order, wrapping around: . useful when the source has multiple audio renditions e.g. original language + dub. the keyhandlerplugin binds , , and the media key to by default. emits: when the track list changes, and the kit's event when the active track changes. checking available tracks read the track list before calling cycle methods if you need to check how many tracks are available: note: the audio track list may not be populated until after the event fires following hls manifest parse. example — subtitle cycle button see also - playback state methods - aspect ratio - keyhandler plugin - subtitleoverlay plugin - player kit — event system

title: HLS
description: HDR-aware ABR, quality level constraints, multi-monitor handling, and how hls.js is wired in.
content: hls the video player uses hls.js for hls playback. the kit's stream adapter wraps hls.js behind the interface. hdr-aware abr is automatic. adaptive bitrate abr abr is on by default. hls.js selects quality levels automatically based on estimated bandwidth. lock to a specific quality level index into : listen for level changes: --- hdr-aware abr on sdr displays, the player filters hdr levels out of the abr selection pool. hls.js will not automatically promote to an hdr level when the display cannot render it. detection is done once at setup via . no configuration is required. on hdr-capable displays, all levels are eligible. multi-monitor handling: when a player window moves across displays e.g. from an hdr monitor to an sdr one, the player re-evaluates display capabilities and constrains the abr pool accordingly. the check runs on the platform event. --- quality level shape returns : --- auth on hls segments the player's auth pipeline injects on every hls manifest and segment request. no hls.js config needed — the intercepts requests before they reach hls.js. see kit — auth & fetch for the full auth pipeline. --- stream registration the player ships an hls stream factory and a native stream factory. the stream registry picks the right one based on the url and browser capabilities: - urls → hls stream via hls.js - other urls → native src register additional stream types: --- custom backend for full control over the element or for non-standard streaming protocols: --- low-latency hls hls.js supports low-latency hls ll-hls. configure via to pass custom hls.js config:

title: Troubleshooting
description: Common video player issues and solutions.
content: video does not play symptoms: stays or immediately becomes after . causes and fixes: 1. no playlist item. verify was called and the array is non-empty. 2. browser autoplay policy blocked. most browsers block without a user gesture. call inside a click handler, or configure the player with to satisfy the autoplay requirement. 3. cors on the hls manifest. the media server must return on and responses. check the browser network tab for blocked requests. 4. hls not supported. the loads hls.js when native hls is unavailable. if returns some sandboxed environments, playback will fail silently. check the browser console for the hls.js error. subtitles do not appear symptoms: subtitle track is selected but nothing renders on screen. causes and fixes: 1. subtitleoverlayplugin not registered. vtt/sidecar subtitles require the plugin. add it before : 2. ass/ssa file without octopusplugin. the subtitleoverlayplugin handles vtt only. for / files, add the octopusplugin and its peer dependency . 3. subtitle url is not reachable. open the field from your in a new browser tab. cors errors in the network tab confirm a server configuration issue. 4. wrong tag. matches against the field on the track. verify the tag e.g. not . quality levels not available symptoms: returns an empty array after . cause: the hls manifest has not been parsed yet when fires. the event fires when the manifest is parsed. subscribe to it instead of polling: audio context not starting web audio plugins symptoms: audiographplugin emits or audio analysis is silent. cause: browsers start in state. the audiographplugin resumes it on the first event, which must occur inside a user gesture. do not call from outside a click/keydown handler. desktopui back button not visible symptoms: the back button in the top bar never appears. cause: the back button only renders when at least one event listener is registered. wire the listener before or after : pip not available symptoms: does nothing. cause: picture-in-picture is only available in chromium-based browsers on desktop and chrome on android. safari uses the proprietary api. firefox does not support the picture-in-picture api on elements at all. drm handshake fails silently symptoms: drmplugin is registered but video fails to play with no event. checks: 1. confirm is set on the drmplugin options. 2. verify the string matches your cdn — widevine is , fairplay is . 3. check the browser console for eme errors. in safari you must also provide a service certificate for fairplay. see also - faq - drm plugin - subtitleoverlay plugin - octopus plugin - audiograph plugin

title: Distributed Playback
description: Group listening, tab-leader coordination, clock synchronization, and drift-correction strategies for synchronized multi-client playback.
content: distributed playback read this when you are building synchronized playback across multiple clients — watch parties, group listening, or any scenario where multiple users or devices must play the same content in lockstep. status note: the nomercy player sdk's first-class group listening feature planned for v2.1 is not yet released. this guide covers the architectural patterns you can implement today using existing kit primitives. the v2.1 will replace the manual setup here. architecture: leader + followers the simplest distributed playback model is a single leader that broadcasts state, and n followers that apply it: --- implementing with signalr or websocket wire the player to a realtime channel via the kit's realtime adapter: connect to the sync channel and apply state: --- drift correction continuous correction without visible seeks: trigger correction on periodic sync ticks from the server every 2–5 seconds is typical. --- clock synchronization system clocks differ between clients. measure the offset before using server timestamps: --- tab leader coordination when a single user has the same player open in multiple tabs e.g. they navigated away and opened a new tab, elect a leader so only one tab is "canonical": --- v2.1 grouplisteningplugin planned when released, the will replace the manual setup above: the existing manual patterns in this guide will remain valid alongside the plugin. --- what to read next - advanced: custom plugin — watch-party-lite plugin for same-device sync - advanced: multi-instance — multiple players on one page - kit — auth & fetch — securing websocket connections with bearer tokens

title: Performance
description: Bundle-size tuning via subpath imports, tree-shake hits to avoid, memory budget for long sessions, leak-test harness, and a production checklist.
content: performance read this when bundle size, memory usage, or long-session stability matter to your app. covers tree-shaking, subpath imports, memory budgeting, and verifying there are no leaks. ------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | | | ~18 kb | ~32 kb kit + all adapters | | | ~28 kb | ~95 kb incl. hls.js, desktopuiplugin, subtitleoverlayplugin | | | ~24 kb | ~60 kb incl. webaudiobackend, lyricsplugin, equalizerplugin | these are rough estimates — the actual size depends on which plugins you register and how your bundler tree-shakes. tree-shake by importing only what you use named imports let bundlers eliminate unused code: subpath imports for kit-level features if you only need the kit no video or music library, import from directly: avoid barrel re-exports in your app hls.js split chunk hls.js is the largest dependency in the video player. configure your bundler to split it into a separate chunk so the player core loads immediately and hls.js loads async: --- tree-shake hit list these patterns prevent effective tree-shaking: | pattern | why it is a problem | fix | | ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | | import 'package'pkgkey audiographpluginequalizerpluginoffthis.onqueueappendassertnolistenerleakthis.on...player.on...settimeoutsetintervalthis.timeoutthis.intervalqueueappendindexeddbbackendoctopusplugineventemitterpluginarrayarrayeventlistenerassertnolistenerleak and the full test harness - advanced: multi-instance — memory budget multiplies per instance - advanced: server-side rendering — ssr reduces initial js parse time

title: Migrating from Other Players
description: Migration notes from hls.js, video.js, Plyr, and Tone.js to the NoMercy Player SDK — concept mapping and API translation.
content: migrating from other players read this when you are switching to the nomercy player sdk from another library. each section maps that library's concepts to the kit's equivalents and highlights the most common translation mistakes. -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | to re-enable abr | | | | key differences - you do not instantiate hls.js directly. if you need custom hls.js config, use — see hls. - auth header injection is handled by the kit's auth pipeline — remove any hls.js or you had. --- from video.js video.js is a full-featured player with its own plugin system and ui. concept mapping | video.js | nomercy video player | | ------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------- | | | | | | | | / | same | | / | same getter/setter | | / | same | | | same | | | same | | | | | / | / | | | same | ui components video.js renders ui inside the player container using its own component system. the nomercy equivalent is . to customize the ui, subclass — do not add elements directly to the container outside the plugin. text tracks --- from plyr plyr is a minimal ui wrapper over the native element. it has no hls support built in — users typically pair it with hls.js manually. concept mapping | plyr | nomercy video player | | ---------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | | | | | / | same | | property | method | | property, 0–1 | method, 0–100 | | property | / / | | | | | | | | | | | | | hls migration if you were wiring hls.js into plyr manually, remove that code. the nomercy player handles hls internally: --- from tone.js audio / music apps tone.js is a web audio framework for musical synthesis and scheduling. it is not a media player — it does not handle queue management, hls streaming, or playlist state. the migration target depends on what you used tone.js for. tone.js as an audio effect chain if you used tone.js for an eq or reverb chain applied to a element, use and instead: tone.js for scheduling if you used to schedule playback events, replace it with the kit's event system: key differences - tone.js is synthesis-first. the nomercy music player is a media player — it streams pre-encoded audio, not synthesize it. - tone.js does not handle hls. the nomercy player does. - tone.js must be started by a user gesture. the nomercy player handles the audiocontext unlock internally. --- what to read next - video quick start — minimal working player in under 30 lines - music quick start — minimal working music player - player migration guide v1 → v2 — if you were on the v1 nomercy player - advanced: custom backend — if you need to preserve hls.js direct access

title: FAQ
description: Frequently asked questions about the NoMercy Video Player.
content: do i need to install hls.js separately? no. hls.js ships as a regular dependency of . your bundler will include it automatically. how do i type my plugin against the player? use the interface rather than the concrete class: how do i set a default subtitle or audio language? pass and bcp-47 tags in : how do i load relative poster urls from a cdn? set in : absolute urls pass through unchanged. why does my subtitle track not render? the field on is the canonical typed field. verify: 1. each entry has , , , and a reachable . 2. for ass/ssa files, add the octopusplugin — vtt sidecar and native texttrack are handled by the subtitleoverlayplugin. 3. check that matches the tag in your track. how do i use thumbnail preview sprites? set on the playlist item. the desktopuiplugin reads this automatically when the user hovers the progress bar: how do i add skip markers for intro or credits? set on the playlist item and register the skipperplugin: listen to to render your own skip button. can i use the player with vue or react? yes. the player is headless and framework-agnostic. mount it into a -attached element: how do i swap the video backend for a custom implementation? pass in config: see video backend adapter. what is the recommended way to handle authentication for private streams? use the kit's config in inherited from . the kit's fetch pipeline injects bearer tokens into all subtitle, font, and poster fetches. see /nomercy-player-kit/auth-fetch. see also - troubleshooting - types reference - videoplaylistitem

your server api, your item shape beyond the typed fields, or any nomercy infrastructure. app-specific glue lives in layer-5 consumer plugins. --- container class system the element and state css classes on are kit-level concerns — the player manages them directly via the container-class mixin. the ui overlay controls, seek bar, menus is the responsibility of the optional . state classes like , , are applied to the container by the kit's container-class-emit mixin when state changes. reads those classes to show/hide ui elements. do not add or prefixed classes to elements from outside the
